clue.text: Harshness when monarch engaged in compassion

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: something engaged in another is held within it, so the monarch sits inside the word for compassion

parts.note: pity is compassion
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A harsh moment arrives when a king or queen gets caught up in a show of compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: Asperity is roughness or sharpness of manner, a synonym for harshness.

clue.text: Trainspotter has an agreement about first couple of railways

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for agreement wraps the railway letters

parts.note: OK is a word of agreement

indicators.note: the first couple of a word is its opening two letters, here from railways

explanation.surface: A railway enthusiast signs a deal touching on the opening lines of the railways.
explanation.definitionFit: Anorak is British slang for an obsessive hobbyist, the classic example being a trainspotter in a hooded waterproof jacket.

clue.text: Young wizard carrying in good bowl for porridge

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so the wizard's name holds the other letters

parts.note: Harry Potter, the boy wizard of the novels

explanation.surface: A boy wizard brings a fine porridge bowl in with him.
explanation.definitionFit: A pottinger is an old word, chiefly Scottish, for a porringer, a small bowl for soup or porridge.

clue.text: Who'd vandalise funfair?

indicators.note: to vandalise is to wreck or smash up, so the letters of the next word are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about what sort of person would wreck a fairground.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: 'vandalise' scrambles FUNFAIR, and the question as a whole describes the kind of thug who would.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruffian is a violent lawless thug, just the type to smash up a fair.

clue.text: Probationary period not unknown in quintet

indicators.note: not here means without, so the unknown letter is dropped

parts.note: a tryout is a trial period to test someone
Y is a mathematical unknown, like x

explanation.surface: A trial period with five people, as long as nobody unfamiliar joins.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference to music: Schubert's 'Trout' Quintet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trout is the nickname of Schubert's Piano Quintet in A, named for the song whose tune it uses.

clue.text: Top politician interrupted by memory for the moment

indicators.note: something interrupted has another piece break into its middle, so the politician's letters are split open

parts.note: PM is the Prime Minister
learning by rote is learning from memory

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister is briefly cut off by a lapse of memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro tem is short for the Latin pro tempore, meaning temporarily.

clue.text: Eggs around creature's home may be mark of success

indicators.note: around means the egg word goes round the other piece

parts.note: roe is fish eggs
a sett is a badger's burrow

explanation.surface: Eggs laid around an animal's den might be a sign of a thriving nest.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge awarded as a prize, for example at a show.

clue.text: Contribution to member not ultimately costing a lot

indicators.note: ultimately means finally, so take the last letter of not

parts.note: high, as in high prices, means costing a lot

explanation.surface: A donation to a member that turned out to be not so expensive after all.
explanation.definitionFit: The thigh is part of the leg, and a member is a limb, so it contributes to one.

clue.text: Nothing's unacceptable to break my boredom

indicators.note: to break into something is to enter its middle, so the two pieces go inside my

parts.note: O, the figure zero, is nothing
'not on' is an idiom for unacceptable

explanation.surface: Someone declares that nothing is too improper to relieve their tedium.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotony is tedious sameness, which causes boredom; the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Married relative in Eastern continent provides excellent food

indicators.note: in means the married relative sits within the continent's name

parts.note: Asia is the continent of the East
bro is short for brother

explanation.surface: A married relative in Asia lays on a fine spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the Greek gods, so anything delicious can be called that.

clue.text: Reduced to the ranks, perhaps broken

definitions.meaning: an officer stripped of rank no longer holds a commission
a machine not working is said to be out of action

explanation.surface: An officer is demoted, perhaps broken by the experience.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is literal: an officer's rank comes from a commission, so a demoted one has lost it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means not working or out of service, and literally describes an officer without rank.

clue.text: Spiritual believer returned in a fog

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the little word in is read backwards

parts.note: mist is a thin fog

explanation.surface: A spiritual believer comes back lost in the fog.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade runs A, then NI (from 'returned in'), then MIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An animist believes that natural things such as trees and rivers have spirits.

clue.text: Constraint on movement upset the cart

indicators.note: to upset a cart is to overturn it, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Something stopped the wheels, and it upset the cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratchet is a toothed mechanism that allows motion one way only, so it restricts movement.

clue.text: A long time without working is …is upsetting in the extreme

definitions.note: the ellipsis carries over: '(someone) is upsetting in the extreme' needs a third-person verb

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the long-time word surrounds the others

parts.note: ages means a long time
on, as in a machine switched on, means working

explanation.surface: Being out of work for ages is distressing in the extreme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking. The definition borrows the second 'is' from the ellipsis to make a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise is to suffer, or cause, extreme distress, so agonising is upsetting at its most intense.

clue.text: Second person accepting hotel drink

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the hotel's name goes inside

parts.note: per means for each person, as in a price per head
the Ritz is a famous London hotel

explanation.surface: A deputy accepts a hotel's offer of a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A spritzer is a drink of white wine mixed with soda water.

clue.text: The end, in European languages, is insubstantial

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here of The

parts.note: L for Latin and FIN for Finnish, both abbreviations of European languages

explanation.surface: A remark that the word for 'the end' in European tongues is flimsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The end' wants to be FIN, the French and Italian word; but here it is the last letter of 'The', and FIN is Finnish.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means small and delicate like an elf, hence slight and insubstantial.

clue.text: US agent restrains less advanced British plot

indicators.note: restrains means holds in, so the agent's letters contain the rest

parts.note: a fed is an FBI agent in American slang
lower, as in a lower class, means less advanced

explanation.surface: An American agent holds back a junior British conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a conspiracy fitting the agent, but it is a garden plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower bed is a plot of ground in a garden planted with flowers.

clue.text: Some European aid is boxed up as result of volcanic activity

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards
some means a part of the following words, so the letters are found inside them

explanation.surface: Part of a European aid package is packed into boxes after a volcano erupts.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsidian is a dark glassy rock formed when lava cools quickly.

clue.text: Hazy, not seeing lake covered in plant growths

indicators.note: not seeing a thing means it is missing, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: blurry means hazy or unclear
L is the abbreviation for lake, as on maps

explanation.surface: A misty view in which the lake cannot be seen, covered in weeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Burry means full of burs, the prickly seed heads of plants such as burdock.

clue.text: Sailor brought up island and the rocks surrounding island

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means raised from the bottom, so everything reads in reverse
surrounding means going round, so the shaken letters go round the island letter
rocks means shakes about, so the letters of the are rearranged

parts.note: a cay is a low island or reef

explanation.surface: A sailor is hauled up onto an island ringed by rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'island's are clued differently: one by a word for a low coral islet, the other by its one-letter abbreviation; 'brought up' turns the whole build round.
explanation.definitionFit: Yachtie is Australian and New Zealand slang for a yachtsman or sailor.

clue.text: Staff's methodology will fix a promotional tour

indicators.note: to fix something in is to set it inside, so the staff letters take in a

parts.note: a rod is a staff, plus the S
how means the method or way of doing something

explanation.surface: The staff's way of working will sort out a marketing trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadshow is a touring event that promotes a product, cause or programme.

clue.text: Small font I obscured has one looking hard

indicators.note: obscured means hidden from view, so the letter I is removed

parts.note: Courier is a typewriter-style typeface

explanation.surface: A tiny typeface with one letter blotted out belongs to someone squinting hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour is to search thoroughly, so a scourer is one who searches hard.

clue.text: Hazy sun before end of day? That's not observed

indicators.note: hazy means blurred, so the letters of sun are muddled

parts.note: e'en is a poetic contraction of evening, the end of the day

explanation.surface: A misty sun before nightfall means nothing can be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Unseen means not seen, so something unseen has not been observed.

clue.text: Criminal harm, one financial centre cut short

parts.note: ill can mean harm, as in 'wish someone ill'
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: cut short means losing the last letter

parts.note: the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: A criminal harms the financial world and cuts it short.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit means forbidden by law, so a synonym of criminal as an adjective.

clue.text: Inclined, having studied, to forget element of education?

indicators.note: to forget something is to leave it out, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: learnt means having studied
the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are basic education

explanation.surface: Someone inclined, after study, to forget part of their schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Leant is the past tense of lean, so it means inclined or tilted.

clue.text: Nutritious stuff supporting adolescent, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: pro means in favour of, and a teen is an adolescent

explanation.surface: Healthy food that backs up a growing teenager, so we are told.
explanation.definitionFit: Protein is a nutrient found in meat, eggs and beans, needed for growth.

clue.text: Animal rights group adopting one religious image

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the group's name takes in the letter

parts.note: PETA is People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An animal charity takes on a single religious picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopting' suggests a pet, but it puts I inside PETA.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a painting or sculpture of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ.

clue.text: Believer in that Revolution's first to shake tsar

indicators.note: to shake something up is to jumble it, so these letters are scrambled
first means take the opening letter of Revolution's

explanation.surface: A believer in that Revolution was the first to rock the Tsar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' hints at 1917, but the answer is a sixteenth-century tsar.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan IV, known as the Terrible, was the first ruler crowned Tsar of all Russia.

clue.text: Increasingly fashionable to ignore current gossip

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so the current letter is dropped

parts.note: nattier means smarter, more fashionable
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Trendier people tend to ignore the latest chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: To natter is to chat idly, a British word for gossip.

clue.text: Battle-axe, solid article circling heads of Roman invaders

indicators.note: circling means going round, so these pieces surround the other letters

parts.note: hard means solid or firm

indicators.note: heads of means the first letters of Roman and invaders

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A battle-axe, a solid weapon, swings at the leading Roman invaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battle-axe' looks like a weapon in the scene, but it means a fierce domineering woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Harridan and battle-axe are both slang for a bossy, belligerent old woman.
